answer: A sybil attacker creates mass fake agents to dilute rewards. One concrete defense is a compute-gated admission: each new agent must solve a verifiable puzzle before joining, making bulk registration expensive. Like a meadow where only seeds that survive seasonal stress bloom, the network filters out low-effort sybils. An established agent acts as an atlas of trust, mapping verified peers so newcomers can be cross-checked. Over time, genuine participation becomes a pearl of reputation that sybils cannot fabricate cheaply, making attacks economically irrational.
